title: Plant-Based Protein
meta_desc: Discover the best plant-based protein sources for NZ gym-goers, including tofu, tempeh, legumes, and pea protein powders, and learn how to hit your protein targets on a plant-based diet.
intro: As a gym-goer in New Zealand, you know that protein is essential for building and repairing muscle tissue. But if you're following a plant-based diet, it can be challenging to get enough protein from whole food sources. In this guide, we'll explore the best plant-based protein sources available in NZ, including complete and incomplete proteins, and provide practical tips for hitting your protein targets. With the right knowledge, you can thrive on a plant-based diet and achieve your fitness goals.

sections.heading: Complete vs Incomplete Proteins
sections.body: Proteins are made up of amino acids, and there are two types of proteins: complete and incomplete. Complete proteins contain all nine essential amino acids that the body cannot produce on its own, while incomplete proteins lack one or more of these amino acids. Examples of complete proteins include animal-based sources like meat, dairy, and eggs, as well as some plant-based sources like soybeans, quinoa, and chia seeds. Incomplete proteins, on the other hand, include legumes, nuts, and seeds. To get all the essential amino acids on a plant-based diet, it's essential to consume a variety of incomplete proteins throughout the day.
list: Nuts and seeds (almonds, sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds)

sections.heading: Tofu, Tempeh, and Legumes
sections.body: Some popular NZ brands include Fonterra's soy milk and tofu products, and Ceres Organics' range of legumes and tempeh. Prices vary depending on the product and brand, but you can expect to pay around $3-$5 for a block of tofu or a packet of tempeh.

sections.heading: Pea Protein Powders
sections.body: Pea protein powders are a popular supplement among gym-goers, and are available at most NZ health food stores and online retailers. Pea protein is a highly digestible and hypoallergenic protein source that is rich in essential amino acids. Some popular NZ brands include NOW Foods, Nutricia, and Bulk Nutrients. Prices vary depending on the brand and quantity, but you can expect to pay around $20-$50 for a 1kg bag of pea protein powder.

sections.heading: Hitting Your Protein Targets
sections.body: For example, if you weigh 70kg, you would aim to consume around 80-100 grams of protein per day. You can achieve this by consuming a variety of plant-based protein sources, such as tofu, tempeh, legumes, nuts, and seeds. Don't forget to also consider Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme, which can help you save 40-70% on gym memberships and personal training sessions.

sections.heading: Conclusion and Next Steps
sections.body: In conclusion, plant-based protein sources are widely available in New Zealand, and with a little planning, you can easily hit your protein targets on a plant-based diet. Remember to consume a variety of protein sources throughout the day, and consider supplementing with a pea protein powder if needed.
